text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Monday:

- The president of the Swiss Jewish Federation, Rolf Bloch, said that the 100 Million Swiss franc fund which has been created to help Holocaust victims should be controlled by a foundation based in Switzerland.

- Swiss banks and diplomats will have a tight agenda this week in New York as the they are expected to take part in a number of hearings and meetings. Among other things, they will discuss how the 100 million franc fund will be administered.

- Some 2,500 people staged a silent demonstration in Berne on Saturday to express their feelings about Switzerland's share of responsibility for the destiny of Jews during World War Two - Two Swiss-based sects, Scientology and Universal Church, plan to use Switzerland's anti-racism laws to silence critics.

- American historian David S. Wyman said in an interview that Switzerland was more generous with regard to the Jews during World War Two than any other country in the World, including the United States. He also expressed criticism on the immigration policy the U.S. applied during the war.
